text:
最近，我终于意识到连续的微积分可能只是人类智力制造的一种工程妥协。

起源是我瑞士的同学给我发来一本书，是一本厚达 1200 页的巨著 A New Kind of Science (NKS)。
这本书的作者，就是我一直关注的天才学者，Stephen Wolfram。

如果你顺着他的思路往下剥，就会发现这种微积分是工程妥协的直觉并非毫无根据，甚至在某种意义上触及了现代物理学与计算理论最深刻的矛盾之一。

1. 为什么说是工程妥协？
在牛顿和莱布尼茨的时代，人类根本没有大规模算力。如果你想预测行星轨道、流体流动或者热量扩散，面对一个由无数微观粒子组成的离散世界，你根本不可能逐个去计算它们的相互作用。
为了获得解析解，我们人类大脑做出了一个极其天才但也极其妥协的假设：

连续性与可微性。

我们把离散的原子抹平，假设空间和时间可以无限分割；把极度复杂的非线性离散迭代，近似为光滑的微分方程；
我们用积分和极限定理，换取了可以用纸笔算出的精确解。

微积分的本质，是用连续光滑的宏观流形，去粗粒化微观上极其复杂、甚至是不可预测的离散状态。它是人类在算力极其匮乏的时代，为了理解世界而不得不做的一种宏观平滑近似。

2. 关于NKS 的离散宇宙观
Wolfram 在 NKS 中展现的逻辑非常粗暴且震撼。
极其简单的离散规则，加上时间的不断迭代，就能自发产生极其复杂的结构与混沌行为。（这里我要提到著名的 Rule 30）。
在传统的微积分视角下，复杂性往往来自于连续方程里的复杂系数或高维耦合x但

在 Wolfram 的视角下，宇宙的底层根本不需要“连续”的概念。空间可能是极其庞大的离散节点图，时间只是图结构的重写规则。
我们所看到的连续时空、广义相对论和量子力学，可能仅仅是这个巨大的离散计算网络在宏观尺度下的热力学极限。
就好比你在屏幕上看到的光滑画面（看似连续），本质上全是一个个独立的像素点（离散）在高速刷新。
微积分研究的是像素平滑后的图像，而 NKS 想直接拆开显示器看电路。

我的解释，应该足够具体了。

3. 连续性遇到计算不可归约性
更深层的震撼在于计算不可归约性。
传统微积分的精髓在于预测未来。
只要给出微分方程和初始条件，带入 t，就能直接用公式算出未来的状态，这就是计算被归约了。
但如果宇宙底层是离散的元胞自动机，很多系统的演化是不可归约的，这意味着不存在任何数学捷径可以让你跨越过程直接预测结果，你唯一的办法就是把规则一步一步运行下去。

微积分之所以看起来无所不能，是因为人类只挑了那些计算可归约的狭窄领域，比如简单轨道、线性波动进行工程应用。
而面对真实世界的大多数复杂系统，像我之前提到的湍流、意识、金融市场、量子引力，连续的微分方程往往迅速陷入发散或奇异点，那正是工程妥协达到极限的警报声。

从连续回到离散，是认知工具在算力纪元的一次彻底解放。
我不可否认，微积分是人类用纸笔征服光滑宏观世界的伟大史诗。
但宇宙的终极底牌，或许真的写在那些极其简单的离散比特与图重写规则之中。

text:
你爱国家，国家爱你吗？

1984年，陕西农民潭福全在河里淘金时捞出一件金灿灿的宝贝，经鉴定，这是西汉鎏金铜蚕，是古代赏赐蚕官的御赐之物，这件国宝后来在一带一路论坛中亮相。

当年，文物贩子曾出价到8000元，但是潭福全没卖，他说：“如果真是文物，就捐给国家”。要知道，那是1984年，普通工人的月工资才几十块钱；那个时候的8000元，是他十几年的收入了。

他专程奔赴西安上交国家，由于他实在太穷，还得向亲戚借了50元路费。

博物馆馆长得到宝物后，奖励了他 —— 70元。

得知他的路费是借来了以后，大善人馆长再给了他30元，总共100大元。

博物馆馆长全家笑而不语。

这件事吧，我有几个评价：

•  这贩子也算是良心商家了，没坑人。可惜农民最后是被正规军给坑了。

•  前阵子中国各大博物馆爆出的事大家都知道吧，其实这些所谓的“爱国”农民，你们把宝物捐给博物馆，馆长转手就卖了，还是流落民间，你却养活了馆长三代人。

现在中国，在自己家里找到文物，不交给国家，牢底坐穿。

在美国，谁拥有土地，宝物就是谁的。

在欧洲大部分国家，国家可以要，但一定给你合理奖金。

2009 年，英国一名业余金属探测爱好者Terry Herbert在农田里发现了 3500 多件金器和银器。最后，博物馆支付了约 328 万英镑 （大约3000万人民币），依据英国《宝藏法》，奖金由发现者和地主Fred Johnson分享。

而自愿上缴的中国农民获得100元人民币。

还是那句话：你爱国家，国家爱你吗？

•  前阵子中国各大博物馆爆出的事大家都知道吧，其实这些所谓的“爱国”农民，你们把宝物捐给博物馆，馆长转手就卖了，还是流落民间，你却养活了馆长三代人。

现在中国，在自己家里找到文物，不交给国家，牢底坐穿。

在美国，谁拥有土地，宝物就是谁的。

在欧洲大部分国家，国家可以要，但一定给你合理奖金。

2009 年，英国一名业余金属探测爱好者Terry Herbert在农田里发现了 3500 多件金器和银器。最后，博物馆支付了约 328 万英镑 （大约3000万人民币），依据英国《宝藏法》，奖金由发现者和地主Fred Johnson分享。

而自愿上缴的中国农民获得100元人民币。

还是那句话：你爱国家，国家爱你吗？

text:
讲个真事。2008年7月，巴西警方冲进里约一间公寓，抄走银行家Daniel Dantas的5块硬盘。但真正的角力，才刚刚开始。

巴西国家犯罪学研究所接手，字典攻击跑了5个月—结果为零。2009年初，案子转给FBI，那边又熬了整整12个月，照样啃不动。直到2010年4月，硬盘原路退回巴西，里面的数据始终纹丝没动。

当年护住这些数据的，是一款叫TrueCrypt的免费开源软件。可2014年，它的开发者突然人间蒸发，官网只扔下一句“别用了”，再没下文。

TrueCrypt倒下的第17天，法国密码学家Mounir Idrassi甩出一个替代品：VeraCrypt。C语言写的，到现在还在更新。2016年，开源技术改进基金会请QuarkSlab把它从头到尾审了一遍，Idrassi在1.19版里把所有漏洞摁死了。

它跟那些商业全盘加密软件，根本不在一个维度上—密钥不在任何人手里，不存云端，法院敲门也没用。单文件、整盘、U盘全支持。还能藏一个隐形卷，刀架脖子上交出去的，只是一堆诱饵。

免费。开源。审计过。数学说了算。

FBI耗了一年都撬不开的锁，才值得装进你的电脑。
🔗 https://t.co/u33Y0yiadM

text:
用第一性原理来重新设计光刻会是什么样子的？网友们在昨天 SpaceX 公开的 Terafab 概念图的正中央看到了“环形加速器”的设计，考虑到整个设施的巨大规模和对称性，Elon 直接回复了“FEL FTW”（自由电子激光）！光源成为整个设施中最重要设计，FEL 的 EUV 光源，与现有 ASML 不同的 3 个方面：

发光方式
• ASML：用激光击打液态锡滴产生等离子体 (LPP)
• FEL：通过粒子加速器将电子加速至光速，直接生成光

安装结构
• ASML：一台曝光设备 = 一台激光器（单独驱动）
• FEL：工厂中央的一台粒子加速器 ➔ 将 EUV 光分配至数十台曝光设备的“中央发电站”方式

性能 & 效率
• ASML：输出功率最高 500W + 需要管理副产物污染
• FEL：无副产物的清洁光源 + 超微细工艺产量最大化

FEL 用粒子加速器（直线加速器或能量回收型 linac/ERL）把电子加速到接近光速，再通过波荡器磁铁阵列让电子“扭动”，从而发出相干、高亮度的 EUV 光。比 ASML 目前使用的 LPP（激光产生等离子体） 光源功率高得多，一台中心源可同时给 8–20 台扫描仪供电，零锡碎屑，镜子更干净、停机更少，波长可调节，而且有更高光子通量。

FEL 解决的是光源，扫描仪（光学、工台、整体系统）仍高度依赖 ASML，这项技术 1970 年代就有，ASML 在 2015 年左右研究过加速器光源，但最终选了 LPP 作为更低风险量产路径。目前 xLight 正在开发集中式 FEL 光源，目标一台给 20 台扫描仪供电，2028 年出原型机。

ASML 使用的 LPP 光源是“模块化、每台机器独立”的务实路径，而 FEL 是“大型共享设施”路径，历史上因体积大、可靠性/稳定性要求高、工业 uptime 难达标而被搁置，但在 Terafab 这种 terawatt 级 AI 芯片（Optimus、Robotaxi、轨道数据中心）超大规模需求下变得极具吸引力。 Elon 用一己之力加速了美国的高端制造✨

text:
前有 PayPal 黑帮，后有 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 黑帮。

2026 年，已经有至少 37 人从 OpenAI 或 Anthropic 出走创业。

从 PayPal 出来的人做出了 Tesla、SpaceX、LinkedIn、YouTube、Yelp、Palantir 等顶尖公司，那这波 AI 创业潮会跑出哪些新星？

几个已经比较清晰的 AI 项目如下：

- @CoreAutoAI（Core Automation）：前 OpenAI 研究副总裁 Jerry Tworek（@MillionInt）创办。
一句话：做世界上最自动化的 AI 实验室，让 AI 自己研究 AI。

- @mirendil（Mirendil）：前 Anthropic 研究员 Behnam Neyshabur（@bneyshabur）等人创办，刚拿 2 亿美元。一句话：做能自我加速的系统，把算力直接变成科学和工程突破。

- @river_ai_inc（River AI）：前 xAI 联合创始人 Igor Babuschkin（@ibab）创办。
一句话：做真正属于个人、由个人塑造的 AI。

- @mathematics_inc（Math Inc）：前 OpenAI 研究员 Jesse Han（@jessemhan）创办。
一句话：用 AI 自动把数学证明变成机器可验证的形式，目标是可验证的超级智能。

-@blackstar_cmptr（Blackstar）：前 OpenAI Codex 工程师 Daniel Edrisian（@DanielEdrisian）创办。

text:
The real reason everybody is worried for Gemini after Jeff (pic related) has left:

Jeff has a keyboard with this little volume wheel thingy (pic2 related) on it. During meetings, he always looks at the pretraining curves, especially signal propagation ones (pic3 paper related). If something trends in the wrong direction, he can type a regex and then use the wheel to change the learning rate of *the specific params matching the regex* smoothly and continuously by turning it slowly (pic4 related).

Effectively, Jeff has been the per-block adaptive learning-rate scheduler for Gemini models. Without this, the loss would always explode as they scale up and train for longer. Now that he's gone, who can take over that job? Sergey? Not Jeff enough. Andy? Can't take the pressure. Nobody! That's the real struggle for Gemini 4 pretraining which is ongoing now, so time is ticking: can they find a new learning-rate scheduler worthy enough, quick enough, before the first spike shows up??

I'm in a GC with the wandb CEO who regularly brags about looking at customer dashboards, so I'll keep y'all updated on any news i hear.

quotedTweet.text:
OpenAI HR told Leopold that a major reason for his firing was the memo he'd sent the board warning how broken OAI's security was.

What happened next makes me even prouder to call him a friend. 

People may have forgotten, but up until 2024, OpenAI had this secret non-disparagement clause in their off-boarding agreement. If you didn’t sign it, they'd clawback all your equity.

As far as I'm aware, there were only two people ever who didn’t sign it - @DKokotajlo, and Leopold Aschenbrenner.

Of all the researchers who left OpenAI before 2024, who had far more to fall back on, Leopold, all of 22 years old, was one of the only ones willing to refuse the golden handcuffs, and say, "I want to preserve my right to talk about safety and security at OAI.”

We have a lot of disagreements, but he's among the most principled and resilient people I know.

text:
最近一直在用据说是对 DeepSeek 优化最好的 Agent 工具：Reasonix，现在已经有3万多 star了，用 Go 写的，性能很好。

这个桌面端 UI 很对我胃口——右边和底部直接把成本、缓存命中、token 等统计展示出来，很有极客风范。关键它没用千篇一律的 Electron，而是用 Golang 的 Wails 框架搭建的，非常轻量。

最具特色的两点：

DeepSeek Prefix-cache 深度对齐：从 Context 维护到 Tool 输出全按 Cache 机制重构，不是表面适配。长会话稳定 90%+ 缓存命中。

独立 Git 之外的 Checkpoint：解决了很多 Agent 只能回退对话不能回退代码，或者搞乱 Git/Worktree 的痛点。代码 + 对话同步 rewind，体验极其干净。

Sergey Brin is the third richest person alive, worth roughly $240 billion, and he just took direct command of Gemini.

He retired in 2019. He owns around 6% of a $3.9 trillion company. He could spend the next 40 years on a yacht without ever checking a price tag.

Instead he's been at the office three to four days a week, in the weeds, writing code. Demis Hassabis confirmed it himself this year, "Sergey has been in the weeds, programming."

The last time Brin was this hands-on, Google was running out of a garage in Menlo Park.

And he fits a pattern. Zuck went founder mode on AI and reorganized all of Meta around superintelligence. Elon started xAI from scratch and built it into a frontier lab in two years. Now Brin, at 52, is personally running the model that decides whether Google wins the next 20 years.

That tells you everything about the size of the prize. Smartphones, cloud, crypto, none of it pulled a retired founder back onto a product team. AI did it in under two years.

A $240 billion man just gave himself a job. The AI war is fully on.

text:
王志文和江珊荧屏上是夫妻，现实中各自安好。王志文坦言：除了我太太以外，江珊真的是我的太太的那种感觉！

很多演员合作过一两次就渐渐失去联系，但有些搭档，即使多年没有再次合作，只要名字放在一起，观众还是会立刻想起那些经典角色。

王志文和江珊，就是这样的一对搭档。

年轻时的他们，在荧屏上演过一对让无数观众记忆深刻的情侣。方言和杜梅之间有争吵、有误会、有冲动，也有年轻人面对爱情时那种笨拙而真诚的情感。两个人的表演没有刻意煽情，却把那个年代普通人的爱情演得格外真实。

也正因为太真实，很多观众后来总会把戏里的感情延伸到戏外，甚至觉得两个人如果真的走到一起，也应该是顺理成章的事情。

他俩的荧屏情侣实在深入人心。王志文甚至承认：除了我太太以外，江珊真的是我的太太的那种感觉......我觉得这是对搭档的最高认可，这种搭档交情也是弥足珍贵。

但人生终究不是电视剧。

王志文后来遇到了自己的妻子陈坚红，组建家庭；江珊也走过了自己的人生道路。两个人没有按照观众期待的剧本继续生活，而是在现实中各自成家、各自工作，也各自经历人生的起起落落。

如今再看他们，已经是另一番模样。

2026年的王志文已经六十多岁，依然没有完全离开影视圈。相比年轻时的高产，如今的他显然更加看重剧本和角色。

今年即将播出的《刑警时刻I》，他饰演的是痕检专家郑道成。这样的角色并不依靠夸张的动作和台词取胜，而更考验演员的经验、眼神和分寸。

这恰恰也是王志文这些年最擅长的东西。

年轻时，他可以靠语言和气场把人物立起来；到了现在，很多时候一个眼神、一个停顿，就足以让观众明白人物心里在想什么。

生活中的王志文也早已从那个荧幕上的“文艺男神”，变成了一个普通的家庭男人。陪妻子逛菜市场、陪家人生活，偶尔被网友偶遇打高尔夫，身上依旧有一种从容的气质。

他和妻子陈坚红的婚姻，也已经走过多年。

而另一边的江珊，同样没有停下脚步。

2026年4月，江珊凭借话剧《德龄与慈禧》获得第三十四届白玉兰戏剧表演艺术奖主角奖。

对于一个演员来说，话剧舞台和影视剧完全是两回事。没有剪辑可以帮你重新来一遍，也没有镜头可以替你隐藏失误。演员必须在现场完成完整的表演，把台词、情绪、节奏和人物状态全部掌握在自己手里。

如今的江珊，早已不是当年那个青春靓丽的荧屏女演员，但她站在舞台上的时候，依然有一种非常强的生命力。

这或许就是好演员最令人佩服的地方。

岁月可以改变容貌，却很难真正带走一个演员对表演的热爱。

王志文和江珊最让人感慨的，其实不是当年的爱情戏，而是他们后来对彼此的态度。

王志文曾用非常特别的方式评价江珊，大意是说，除了自己的妻子之外，江珊身上有一种“妻子的感觉”。

这句话如果放在年轻时候，很容易被观众理解成爱情；可是到了今天，再回头看，它更像是一种对老搭档的认可。

因为两个人曾经一起演过最亲密的角色，所以彼此之间留下的那种熟悉感，是后来任何搭档都很难复制的。

他们太了解彼此的表演方式，也知道对方在镜头前一个眼神、一个停顿意味着什么。

但这种熟悉，并不一定非要变成爱情。

有时候，能够在年轻时共同留下经典，在多年以后依然尊重彼此、欣赏彼此，然后各自拥有自己的家庭和人生，反而是一种更成熟、更难得的关系。

王志文如今有自己的家庭和生活，江珊也有自己的事业和人生。

他们不需要再去证明什么，也不需要为了满足观众的想象重新走到一起。

偶尔在公开场合遇见，两个人大方打招呼；其中一人获得成绩，另一人送上祝福。

没有暧昧，没有刻意炒作，也没有所谓的“意难平”。

只有一种经历过岁月之后的体面。

年轻的时候，我们喜欢看方言和杜梅吵架，总觉得两个人明明相爱，却偏偏不会好好表达。

多年以后再看王志文和江珊，才突然明白：那是电视剧里的故事，而真正的人生，是两个人从戏里走出来以后，各自把自己的日子过好。

最好的搭档，不一定要成为夫妻。

最深的缘分，也不一定要以爱情收场。

有些人曾经陪你完成人生中最精彩的一段表演，后来各自走向不同的舞台，却依然能够在多年以后想起彼此时，心里留着一份欣赏和尊重。

这或许才是王志文和江珊最好的结局：

戏里，他们曾经深爱过。

戏外，他们各自幸福。

而多年以后，当观众再次提起他们，记住的依然是那个时代最真实、最动人的荧屏情侣。

最近 skills 生态明显在爆发。

一批工程师级的 Agent Skills 仓库集中冒头,方向出奇一致:
给 AI 编程 agent 装上一套高质量的工程规范。

· obra/superpowers —— 26.9 万 star
· mattpocock/skills —— 20.9 万
· addyosmani/agent-skills —— 8.4 万
· PrimeIntellect-ai/prime-agent —— 6.8k

拿 addyosmani 那个说,它把 24 个 skill 按软件生命周期铺开:
搞清楚做什么、拆解、编码、验证、评审门禁、上线。

最戳我的一个细节:每个 skill 里都列了一张「agent 常用来跳步的借口」
清单,专门治它偷工减料。README 里举的例子就是那句最耳熟的
"I'll add tests later"。

这波解决的,是 Vibe Coding 和生产级代码之间那道质量鸿沟。
光让模型能写、写得又快又爽,离能上线还差一整套工程纪律。

Skills 已经成为继 MCP 之后的下一个生态热点,
标准化的是「怎么把活干对」。

text:
I wrote my first message into the Bitcoin blockchain yesterday. Block 961,344 and block 961,345. It'll be there as long as Bitcoin is.

Most people have never seen a message written into the Bitcoin blockchain. Most wouldn't know how to put one there if they wanted to.

So I built both. And ironically I finished it on the same day BIP 110 starts signaling 😅

• Read the chain. 3,034 human readable messages found, grouped into 911 distinct ones, searchable by keyword and date
• Write to the chain. Type a message, pay a Lightning invoice, and it lives on Bitcoin forever

No terminal, no node, no code. Just type and pay it’s very simple. 

Right now I've only scanned the last 12,796 blocks. If people want to dig further back into Bitcoin's history, I'll expand it.

To be clear about what this is
• 80 bytes of text only, no pictures, no files
• CSAM and illegal content get refused before you ever see an invoice
• One 80 byte OP_RETURN in a roughly 200 vbyte transaction. That's an 83 byte output script, exactly the long standing standardness limit Core relays by default and the same ceiling BIP 110 would set at the consensus level

I know some people won't love this. But plenty of folks would like to leave a few words that outlive them, and I'd rather they do it safely than not at all ⚡

Search "bitcoin radar" on the Apple App Store it’s free to download, link in the comments 👇

text:
Grey-market peptides are better than you’ve been led to believe.

One academic study produced a "41% to 71% peptide failure” headline from one voluntary testing program.

We reanalyzed 64,787 public laboratory reports.

Here’s what the larger record shows:

→ 99.31% contained the peptide named on the label.

→ 93.08% were no more than 10% below the labelled dose—or were at/above it.

→ 98.99% were not severely short-filled, meaning 40% or more below the labelled dose.

And the failures were heavily concentrated.

Depending on the problem measured, just 0.53%–2.43% of vendors accounted for half of the results where:

• the labelled peptide was not found
• purity was below 95%
• the vial contained 40%+ less than labelled

That does not look like one uniformly unsafe market.

It looks like a largely high-performing market with a small, identifiable tail of poor suppliers.

The grey market’s greatest strength is community testing:

Buyers fund independent laboratory tests.
COAs are shared publicly.
Bad batches become visible.
Vendors can be compared.
Communities can react in real time.

In major testing sources, low-purity and underfill rates fell as this surveillance network expanded.

Pharma has mandatory manufacturing controls.

The grey market has a different strength: public, sample-level evidence that buyers can actually inspect.

The answer is more testing, more shared reports and faster visibility into the vendors that fail.

See the complete 64,787-record analysis:

https://t.co/xfb2N09om8

4、Lovart 在继续跌。可惜没看到 LibTV 的数据。对陈冕，始终敬佩不起来。可能是我自己的问题。

有意思的是，昨天字节一高级 HRBP 加我微信，跟我说：一鸣偶尔也是非常感性的。

庸俗的创业圈。身处其中。都没时间去看奥德赛。没意思。

text:
给所有 Coding Agent 加速！

NanoNets 开源 Graft ，让 Claude Code / Cursor / Codex / Gemini 更懂你的代码库

每次任务 Agent 都要从零摸一遍代码库，烧 token、烧时间、还容易跑偏。

Graft 的解法：
1.一次性把仓库建成「可读的上下文图」（linked markdown 节点）

2.每个节点用大白话解释系统、API、概念，而不是堆符号列表

3.图就躺在 repo 里（graft/ 文件夹），跟代码一起走 git，无需额外服务器

实测效果（Claude Code）：
1.工具调用 ↓46%
2.Token ↓42%
3.时间 ↓60%
4.SWE-bench Verified 正确率 65% → 75%（+10pts）
最高可达 4× 更便宜、3× 更快，正确性不降反升！

一行安装：

bash
npm i -g @nanonets/graft && graft init

还得是日本老哥会玩🌸

非常有趣，非常好玩😄

大家可以尝试看看上传自己图片然后输入下面提示词🎨

 Seedance 2.5 prompt 👇

【风格】日本大型综艺水上闯关特别节目（Japanese TV Game Show，Live-Action Broadcast），多机位实时转播，4K真实摄影（Photorealistic），高饱和夏日色彩，全片实时无慢动作

【时长】30秒

【场景】晴天户外大型休闲泳池闯关赛道，五关从左到右一字排开。第一关：5米高木制起跳台，头顶缆绳挂带滑轮的泰山绳。第二关：水面上一块直径3米的红黄配色圆形浮盘，装在水下轴上持续匀速自转，表面湿滑。第三关：四块间距不等的方形跳板浮块，随水波上下起伏。第四关：一面倾斜的蓝色湿滑爬坡墙，顶端垂下几根抓绳。第五关：横架在水面上的巨大黄色圆柱管道，湿润反光的乙烯基表面印红色火焰纹，靠电机持续匀速自转，粗细刚好能被手臂和双腿环抱，右端连着小型终点台，正下方是清澈泳池、无安全垫。背景棕榈树、大型水滑梯、灯架、解说席、坐满观众的临时观众席。全片推进方向一律从左到右。

【角色】挑战者（成年日本女性，结实健康的运动体型，穿衣服）

【固定项】五关的位置尺寸颜色与连接关系全片不变；画面中始终只有一名挑战者；开场头发和衣服是干的，只有落水后才自然湿透；圆形浮盘和黄色管道在出现的所有镜头中都必须是持续转动的

[00:00-00:03] 镜头1：泰山绳蹬出（Eye-level Medium → Wide Pull-back，ENG Camera）

画面：她双手握住绳子站在5米高台边缘，脚趾扣住台沿。

台词：「絶対クリアします！」（我一定要通关！）

动作：蜂鸣器一响，她用力向前蹬出，滑轮沿缆绳向右滑行，身体在水面上方划出钟摆轨迹，头发被风向后带起。

解说：「まずはターザンロープ！」（首先是泰山绳！）

音效：起跳蜂鸣器、滑轮滑行声、全场欢呼。

[00:03-00:07] 镜头2：转盘落地（Fixed Side Shot）

镜头：浮盘侧面固定机位，人、绳、转盘同框。

画面：红黄配色的圆形浮盘正在水面上持续匀速自转，湿滑表面反光。

动作：她松开绳子落上转盘，双脚一沾就被转盘带着向侧后方滑开，她张开双臂原地小碎步反向蹬踏抵消转速，膝盖弯曲重心压低，晃了两下站住。

表情：眉毛猛地扬起，牙关咬紧，随即咧嘴笑。

解说：「回転盤だ！耐えた！」（是转盘！撑住了！）

音效：转盘轴的低频嗡嗡声、鞋底摩擦声、爆发的欢呼。

[00:07-00:12] 镜头3：跳板连跳（Dolly Track L→R）

镜头：轨道摄像机与前进方向平行，从左向右跟移。

画面：四块方形浮块随水波上下起伏，间距不等。

动作：她从转盘边缘起跳，连续四次单脚点跳跨过浮块。第二块踩偏，浮块猛地下沉，她上身前扑双臂大幅画圈找平衡，右脚在水面拍出一片水花后勉强蹬上第三块，最后一跳双脚落上第四块。

台词：「危なっ……！」（好险……！）

解说：「二枚目で崩れた！でも繋いだ！」（第二块踩崩了！但接住了！）

音效：浮块入水的闷响、水花声、观众此起彼伏的惊呼。

[00:12-00:17] 镜头4：湿滑爬坡墙（Front 3/4 Medium Shot）

镜头：正面斜前方中景，人、坡墙、顶端抓绳同框。

画面：蓝色倾斜坡墙表面淌着水，反着光。

动作：她助跑冲上坡墙，跑了三步鞋底打滑往下溜了一截，她立刻扑倒身体双手扒住墙面，指尖抠住表面纹路，再次蹬腿爬升，右手抓到顶端垂下的抓绳，双臂发力把自己拽上顶端。

表情：脖子绷出线条，额头挤出横纹，大口喘气。

台词：「よいしょ、よいしょ……！」（嘿咻、嘿咻……！）

解说：「滑る壁！腕だけで登った！」（打滑的墙！全靠手臂爬上去了！）

音效：湿墙面的摩擦声、绳子绷紧声、全场掌声。

[00:17-00:21] 镜头5：抱上转动的柱子（Rear Side Fixed Shot）

镜头：稍靠后的固定侧机位，能看清管道正在转。

画面：黄色圆柱管道靠电机持续匀速自转，湿润的乙烯基表面上有一层水膜，红色火焰纹随转动不断卷过画面。

动作：她从坡顶跳下俯身跨上管道根部，胸腹、双臂、双腿同时箍住。管道的自转立刻把她整个人往右侧带过去，她跟着管道的转向反向调整重心，交替小幅挪动手臂和双腿往终点蹭。

台词：「えっ、回ってる！？」（诶，它在转！？）

解说：「回転丸太だ！これが最難関！」（是转动的圆木！这是最难的一关！）

音效：电机低频转动声、湿乙烯基的摩擦声。

[00:21-00:26] 镜头6：被转翻·终点前极限（Front Close-up → Medium Pull-back）

镜头：终点侧正面特写缓慢拉到中景，机位轴线不变。

动作：管道持续转动，把她的身体一点点往右侧带翻，她的重心越过管道最高点后再也压不回来。右腿先脱开在空中扑腾一下，接着右手也脱开朝终点台伸出，全身重量吊在左臂和左腿上，随管道继续向右转。

表情：太阳穴青筋鼓起，手臂肌肉发抖，眼睛瞪圆。

台词：「もうダメ、待って……！」（不行了，等等……！）

解说：「回転に負けた！あと少し！」（被转动打败了！就差一点！）

承接：右手指尖距终点台约20厘米，左手仍贴着仍在转动的管道。

[00:26-00:28] 镜头7：终点前落水（Fixed Side Shot）

镜头：管道侧面固定机位，管道、伸出的右手、终点台、正下方水面同框。

动作：管道再转过一点，支撑的左手被转到管道下侧后滑脱，她身体保持侧向顺重力直坠入泳池，砸起大片水花。管道在她落下后仍在原位持续自转。

台词：「あーっ！」（啊——！）

解说：「落ちた！丸太に回されたー！」（掉下去了！被圆木转翻了！）

音效：豪爽的入水声、观众的惊呼。

[00:28-00:30] 镜头8：水面反应收尾（Water-level Close-up，Static）

镜头：水面高度正面特写，机位静止，优先表现脸部。

动作：她从水里探出脸和肩膀，湿发一缕缕贴在脸颊上，抹了一把脸，看向终点方向皱起眉，双手拍了一下水面。

台词：「悔しい！」（好懊恼！）

动作：视线转回镜头，皱着的眉松开，转成害羞的笑，肩膀缩了一下。背景里黄色管道仍在慢慢转。

[00:21-00:26] 镜头6：被转翻·终点前极限（Front Close-up → Medium Pull-back）

镜头：终点侧正面特写缓慢拉到中景，机位轴线不变。

动作：管道持续转动，把她的身体一点点往右侧带翻，她的重心越过管道最高点后再也压不回来。右腿先脱开在空中扑腾一下，接着右手也脱开朝终点台伸出，全身重量吊在左臂和左腿上，随管道继续向右转。

表情：太阳穴青筋鼓起，手臂肌肉发抖，眼睛瞪圆。

台词：「もうダメ、待って……！」（不行了，等等……！）

解说：「回転に負けた！あと少し！」（被转动打败了！就差一点！）

承接：右手指尖距终点台约20厘米，左手仍贴着仍在转动的管道。

[00:26-00:28] 镜头7：终点前落水（Fixed Side Shot）

镜头：管道侧面固定机位，管道、伸出的右手、终点台、正下方水面同框。

动作：管道再转过一点，支撑的左手被转到管道下侧后滑脱，她身体保持侧向顺重力直坠入泳池，砸起大片水花。管道在她落下后仍在原位持续自转。

台词：「あーっ！」（啊——！）

解说：「落ちた！丸太に回されたー！」（掉下去了！被圆木转翻了！）

音效：豪爽的入水声、观众的惊呼。

[00:28-00:30] 镜头8：水面反应收尾（Water-level Close-up，Static）

镜头：水面高度正面特写，机位静止，优先表现脸部。

动作：她从水里探出脸和肩膀，湿发一缕缕贴在脸颊上，抹了一把脸，看向终点方向皱起眉，双手拍了一下水面。

台词：「悔しい！」（好懊恼！）

动作：视线转回镜头，皱着的眉松开，转成害羞的笑，肩膀缩了一下。背景里黄色管道仍在慢慢转。

音效：全场大欢呼和掌声推到最高点。

【音响】

全片薄铺一层日本大型综艺特别节目风格的快节奏游戏秀BGM。观众欢呼、掌声、笑声、起跳蜂鸣器、滑轮滑行声、转盘和电机的低频转动声、浮块入水声、湿墙面摩擦声、湿乙烯基摩擦声、水滴声、入水声，各自与对应动作同步。解说和挑战者说自然清晰的日语，除指定说话者外不让任何人出声，台词与口型同步。台词期间BGM和欢呼自然压低，不盖过人声，不加多余旁白。

【机位与剪辑】

自然多机位电视转播，只用硬切。混用ENG摄像机、钢丝摄像机、轨道摄像机、水面高度摄像机、长焦画角，每个区间只用指定的那一种机位运动。转盘和管道所在的镜头必须选用能明确看出转动方向的构图。维持180度轴线规则和从左到右的推进方向。禁止超高速运镜、剧烈旋转、冲击变焦、过度变焦、无人机式急转弯，禁止慢动作、重播、定格、时间跳跃。

【全片禁止】

全片保持脸部、发型、体型、服装、肤色、体格、左右手脚数量一致。手脚与各关卡的接触和脱离严格按时间线顺序发生，真实表现重力、惯性、打滑、自转、水花。转动的道具不得出现静止帧或忽然停转。不出现瞬移、位置倒退、空中静止、身体变形、手脚增减、物体增殖、穿透道具、背景替换。以健康清爽的运动综艺风格呈现，服装不脱落、不破损、不透明、不过度位移。不出现真实存在的节目名、电视台名、企业名、赞助商名、商标，不出现字幕、节目logo、台标、水印、无意义文字、乱码。

text:
Hi @Ledger @Trezor @FoundationHQ @BlockstreamJade @KeystoneWallet @Bitkey 

I created an offline entropy method where you can use a pair of d8 dice and a booklet with 32 pages of 8x8 grids to quickly generate BIP39 words directly, all that’s needed is a checksum calculator

It’s very beginner friendly, easy to onboard newbs. Cheap to mass print booklets and buy wholesale d8 dice.

I’ve realized there’s a security benefit to this: In your hardware wallets you can encode the same method of entropy generation with d8 dice rolls. The user inputs the rolls to your HWW, you return the word, the user can MANUALLY VERIFY it’s the same word on the booklet, no need to test on a second HWW from different vendor. 

Then they can learn to trust your HWW and have generate seed phrases quickly.

Hope y’all can consider my proposal! The booklet docs etc are all in the Github Repos attached in article.

text:
Why wealth inequality is more important than income?

Another excellent article by the guru of data analysis (John Burn-Murdoch of the FT), where he eloquently explained why wealth inequality is more critical today than more conventional income coefficients. It is perfectly in tune with my thoughts and how I addressed this issue in my recent books, especially “The Twilight Before the Storm”.

To quote from the article:

“If macroeconomic conditions lead everyone’s wealth to double, relative shares for the top and bottom are unchanged. But if that wealth boom is not matched by a corresponding rise in wages (the ability to earn one’s way up that distribution), suddenly the same-sized relative gaps matter much more, reshaping how the economy both feels and functions.

In a society where the gap between the comfortably off and the just-getting-started can be crossed in a decade or two of hard work, success feels attainable and incentives are strong. When those gaps are so wide that even a lifetime of striving doesn’t offer the prospect of feeling you’ve ‘made it’, things start to break down.”

As he illustrated, most western economies have gone from requiring 10 to 15 years of savings to move from the bottom 25% to the top, today, this extends to 40 years or longer. In economic jargon, the transfer of value from labor to capital has been accelerating at a pace that cannot be bridged through wages and household chattels. 

Four points to add:

1. To find a consistent international database, John limited himself to the top 1%. However, the real story, at least in the US, is not top 1% but top 0.1% or 135,000 households. This small cohort is rapidly pulling away from the next 0.9%. According to the Fed data, top 0.1% controls 14.5% of national wealth or $188m per household, compared to 12% or $88m a decade ago, and 8.6% in 1989. The bottom 50% are worth $60,000 or 2.5% of national wealth. This is more extreme than during the Gilded Age.

2. The primary driver is what my books describe as the “Fujiwara Effect”: merger and reinforcement of two hurricanes of highly disruptive Information Age and equally disruptive deep Financialization, which redefine the role of capital and labor, their interactions and relative values.

3. Although in the midst of technological and financial revolutions, relative returns on capital do increase, there are only three ways to rebalance: violent destruction, redistribution policies or sustainable productivity rebound. Given that the latter will take time, in the short to medium term it leaves only destruction and distribution to defang polarization.

4. Finally, as John highlights, unlike the Gilded Age, today’s 0.1% tend to be more vocal and active in their attempts to capture and reshape institutions and public opinion.

Wealth redistribution is coming one way or another. It is just a question of balance between violence and proactive policies.

Views expressed are solely my own and do not reflect views of my employer.

As he illustrated, most western economies have gone from requiring 10 to 15 years of savings to move from the bottom 25% to the top, today, this extends to 40 years or longer. In economic jargon, the transfer of value from labor to capital has been accelerating at a pace that cannot be bridged through wages and household chattels. 

Four points to add:

1. To find a consistent international database, John limited himself to the top 1%. However, the real story, at least in the US, is not top 1% but top 0.1% or 135,000 households. This small cohort is rapidly pulling away from the next 0.9%. According to the Fed data, top 0.1% controls 14.5% of national wealth or $188m per household, compared to 12% or $88m a decade ago, and 8.6% in 1989. The bottom 50% are worth $60,000 or 2.5% of national wealth. This is more extreme than during the Gilded Age.

2. The primary driver is what my books describe as the “Fujiwara Effect”: merger and reinforcement of two hurricanes of highly disruptive Information Age and equally disruptive deep Financialization, which redefine the role of capital and labor, their interactions and relative values.

3. Although in the midst of technological and financial revolutions, relative returns on capital do increase, there are only three ways to rebalance: violent destruction, redistribution policies or sustainable productivity rebound. Given that the latter will take time, in the short to medium term it leaves only destruction and distribution to defang polarization.

4. Finally, as John highlights, unlike the Gilded Age, today’s 0.1% tend to be more vocal and active in their attempts to capture and reshape institutions and public opinion.

Wealth redistribution is coming one way or another. It is just a question of balance between violence and proactive policies.

Views expressed are solely my own and do not reflect views of my employer.

$PATH  is still under the radar, known as a fallen out of touch RPA software company. They have recently pivoted to agenticAI (and combined with traditional RPA) have an orchestration platform that will unlock the potential of LLM.

Path’s agentic AI and orchestration capabilities (centered on Maestro and Agent Builder) represent a meaningful step toward monetizing AI in the application/process layer beyond pure picks and shovels infrastructure. The current AI phase is still heavily infrastructure-driven (GPUs, cloud compute, foundational models). True broader monetization occurs when AI reliably drives business outcomes. Cost savings, revenue lift, process transformation, at enterprise scale. That requires moving from isolated model calls or chatbots to coordinated, governed, long running workflows that mix AI agents, deterministic robots/RPA, APIs, and humans.

Maestro (agentic orchestration) the control plane that models processes, coordinates UiPath agents, third party agents (OpenAI, Microsoft Copilot/Foundry, Google Vertex, Salesforce, etc.), robots, and humans. It handles long running cases, state, retries, exceptions, human in the loop, governance via an AI Trust Layer, and KPI monitoring. Deterministic robots handle reliable, rules based steps agents handle judgment/unstructured work and humans intervene on exceptions.

Customers are already seeing real ROI. Multi million dollar savings in claims, purchase to pay, document processing, pricing, and other processes. Path is seeing larger expansion deals when AI/agentic capabilities are included (3–6× larger) and faster time to value.

Agentic/AI features appear in a high percentage of top deals and Path has reached GAAP profitability with agentic momentum. ARR growth is solid (double digits), with a pipeline for exponential revenue growth with agentic positioned as a key expansion driver.

This is my largest position, and my highest conviction bet. I think if you believe in the AI story than you also must believe that Agentic ai and orchestration is the future for growth unlock.

Maestro (agentic orchestration) the control plane that models processes, coordinates UiPath agents, third party agents (OpenAI, Microsoft Copilot/Foundry, Google Vertex, Salesforce, etc.), robots, and humans. It handles long running cases, state, retries, exceptions, human in the loop, governance via an AI Trust Layer, and KPI monitoring. Deterministic robots handle reliable, rules based steps agents handle judgment/unstructured work and humans intervene on exceptions.

Customers are already seeing real ROI. Multi million dollar savings in claims, purchase to pay, document processing, pricing, and other processes. Path is seeing larger expansion deals when AI/agentic capabilities are included (3–6× larger) and faster time to value.

Agentic/AI features appear in a high percentage of top deals and Path has reached GAAP profitability with agentic momentum. ARR growth is solid (double digits), with a pipeline for exponential revenue growth with agentic positioned as a key expansion driver.

This is my largest position, and my highest conviction bet. I think if you believe in the AI story than you also must believe that Agentic ai and orchestration is the future for growth unlock.

text:
What do I believe is true about the Book of Mormon after 20+ years of reading it?

The Book of Mormon is the only scripture on earth written by the losers of one American apocalypse to the finalists of the next.

REDISCOVERY AMERICA: A Vision of Transformative Renewal and Inclusive Flourishing

America stands at a crossroads. Political and ideological divisions, weakening trust, and widening socioeconomic disparities have left the nation fragmented and fragile. The question before us is not merely whether America can survive, but whether it can rediscover the core vision and fundamental values of its beginnings and rebound to even greater heights of purpose and promise.

Even more crucial is whether we, Christians—whose predecessors contributed significantly to the nation’s founding—can rediscover our identity and calling, take the initiative in addressing perceived wrongs, and be agents of redemptive transformation within the nation.

Debates about the beliefs of the Founders and the intended character of the nation will continue. Yet it seems undeniable that the establishment of the United States was profoundly influenced by a biblical worldview and Christian values. Even more striking is the extent to which American history echoes the biblical story of the founding of ancient Israel—with shared themes including theistic motivations, liberation from servitude, the displacement of native peoples, a sense of providential purpose, and the prospect of severe consequences in the event of failure.

This is not intended to equate America with Israel, or “replace” the latter with the former, or present a Christianized America as the promised kingdom of biblical eschatology. Rather, the intention is to acknowledge realities that should invite deeper introspection and greater intentionality in discussions and actions concerning our country’s direction.

The birth of a nation, like that of a child, is rarely tidy. It is often marked by struggle and travail. If we could bring forth our children in a less messy way, we would do so. But the path of anguish and blood is what nature has bequeathed to us. This analogy offers a sobering perspective from which the founding of America may be reexamined, and the implications should humble us without paralyzing us. It becomes even more compelling when we consider the significant role the nation has played in the continuing evolution of human civilization.

We cannot undo the nation’s past, but we can decide how we move forward from the present. Endless recrimination or self-flagellation will not heal us. But humility, responsibility, and courage can help us use the uncommon privilege we have inherited to make the land we possess a better place for all its inhabitants and a model for the rest of the world.

Not everyone will agree with our perspective, but that should not hinder us from pursuing a responsible and redemptive vision. Liberty is one of the fundamental values of the United States, affording us the freedom to pursue our aspirations within the bounds of the law.

We cannot reestablish America, but we can rediscover the essence of its founding. More importantly, we whom our Lord described as the “salt of the earth” and the “light of the world” can rediscover this identity and calling as agents of transformative impact (Matthew 5:13–16). We can recover the 1630 vision of a “city upon a hill” articulated by Puritan governor John Winthrop, who called the Massachusetts Bay colonists to live in covenant with God as a “model of Christian charity.” We can reimagine the American Dream in a way that authentically witnesses to the redemptive love of God in Christ and promotes transformative renewal and inclusive flourishing.

We may not transform the entire nation, but through lived witness, we can spread the hope that somewhere within the unfolding of divine providence lies the possibility of a human civilization that embodies dimensions of human fulfillment beyond anything we have ever imagined (1 Corinthians 2:9–10).

This is the vision of Rediscovery Community, and we invite you to join us in our pursuit of redemptive transformation.

_________________________
Rediscovery Community is a network community of Christians seeking a contemporary recovery of the mutual responsibility, integrated engagement, and social credibility of the earliest believers as a path toward transformative cultural renewal and inclusive socioeconomic flourishing.  Follow us: https://t.co/1M0C61Pq9f . To learn more, visit our website: https://t.co/8fp06h9fwb .

text:
The Argument from Dog

Fifteen thousand years ago, somewhere between the ice retreating and agriculture arriving, humans and wolves made a deal. We fed them, they watched our camps, and over enough generations the watching turned into something closer to devotion. No other animal on earth has been bred this specifically, this relentlessly, for one trait: loyalty. Every culture that has ever kept a dog has arrived at roughly the same conclusion about what dogs are for and what they mean to us.

So it's worth asking what the book claiming to speak for the being who designed dogs in the first place actually says about them.

Not much good, as it turns out. When Ahab dies, dogs lick up his blood in the street, a detail meant as a fitting punishment. Jezebel's fate is worse still, her body is left for the dogs to eat, and the writer lingers on it as though justice has finally arrived. When Goliath sizes up David, his insult of choice is to ask if he's being approached like a dog. Proverbs reaches for a dog eating its own vomit as the sharpest image available for a fool who won't learn. Paul warns the Philippians to watch out for "the dogs," meaning the people he disagrees with theologically. And when Revelation finally draws the gates of the New Jerusalem, dogs are named among those left standing outside, filed next to sorcerers and murderers.

A thousand years of writers, and not one of them manages a sentence of real warmth toward a dog.

Compare that to Homer, working centuries before most of the New Testament existed. As many of us have been reminded by Nolan's recent film, The Odyssey, an old dog named Argos waits twenty years for his owner to come home. He's flea-bitten, dying, lying on a dung heap, ignored by everyone. Odysseus walks past him in disguise, unrecognized by every human in the palace. Argos knows him instantly, lifts his head, wags his tail, and dies having seen his master one last time. This supposedly "primitive and pagan" epic gives dogs the single most affecting scene in ancient literature. The text that claims to channel a perfect, all-knowing creator can't produce anything within a thousand miles of it.

So, if the Bible really came from a mind standing outside culture, one that made every creature and loved what it made, why does its attitude toward dogs read exactly like the attitude of Iron Age herders who saw feral strays eating their garbage and their goats? Not one degree warmer. Not one flash of the affection a shepherd might plausibly have felt for the animal actually working his flock beside him.

The obvious answer is that these are human authors, writing from inside their own time and place, and their prejudices about scavenger dogs made it onto the page along with everything else their ancient culture and circumstances produced. But if the text is tracking Bronze Age livestock economics instead of some timeless moral order handed down from outside history, then it's doing exactly what every other human document does: reflecting the people who wrote it, not a mind that transcends them. Most readers can accept that in the abstract. It's a different thing to feel it, and dogs happen to be one of the rare cases where a modern reader can feel it immediately, because we already know, in our bones, what a good dog is worth.

Man's best friend spent three thousand years as scripture's favorite insult. We all know "who's a good dog." I think it's clear that the God of the Bible does not.

text:
哇靠，原来Google 这次的人事变动公告根本不是什么管理层正常变动和交接啊，

官方叙事很干净：Demis Hassabis 辞去 DeepMind CEO，转任主席兼首席科学家，继续领导 Isomorphic Labs，日常运营交给 Koray Kavukcuoglu。
同一天，Jeff Dean、Sanjay Ghemawat、Oriol Vinyals、Quoc Le 集体离职创办 Discovery Loop，谷歌还投了钱。

两件事放在同一天发，本身就是一个信号。

@Pathfounders  挖出的内幕是：Hassabis 本来想跟 Dean 他们一起走，但谷歌管理层判断双核心同时出走会导致股价崩盘，于是说服他接受这个新设的 Chair 角色，等组织稳定后再体面退出。预测他可能在一年内真正离开。

为什么这个说法可信度很高。

第一，DeepMind Chair 是个临时发明的头衔，真正重要的职位早就存在，凭空造一个升职，太像危机公关了。

第二，Hassabis 自己反复说他是科学家不是产品经理，至少一年前就想减少执行职责，这个方向和被迫留下完全不矛盾。

第三，即使是管理过的版本，股价当天都跌了 4% 到 5%，抹掉将近两千亿美元市值，如果同时宣布他也走，市场解读会变成谷歌 AI 核心团队瓦解。

这才是这件事真正让人震惊的地方，

大公司做前沿 AI 的结构性矛盾已经集中爆发了，顶尖人才越来越受不了官僚、资源争夺和短期产品压力。

Jeff Dean 这种在谷歌干了 27 年的传奇都走了，说明问题不是个人层面的，是系统层面的。

AI 现在是 Alphabet 估值的核心，管理层必须优先考虑股价和舆论，而不是研究最优结构，结果就是这种软着陆安排——既留住品牌和影响力，又避免公开撕裂。

DeepMind 作为伦敦独立力量的时代，基本结束了。

哇靠，原来Google 这次的人事变动公告根本不是什么管理层正常变动和交接啊，

官方叙事很干净：Demis Hassabis 辞去 DeepMind CEO，转任主席兼首席科学家，继续领导 Isomorphic Labs，日常运营交给 Koray Kavukcuoglu。
同一天，Jeff Dean、Sanjay Ghemawat、Oriol Vinyals、Quoc Le 集体离职创办 Discovery Loop，谷歌还投了钱。

两件事放在同一天发，本身就是一个信号。

@Pathfounders  挖出的内幕是：Hassabis 本来想跟 Dean 他们一起走，但谷歌管理层判断双核心同时出走会导致股价崩盘，于是说服他接受这个新设的 Chair 角色，等组织稳定后再体面退出。预测他可能在一年内真正离开。

为什么这个说法可信度很高。

第一，DeepMind Chair 是个临时发明的头衔，真正重要的职位早就存在，凭空造一个升职，太像危机公关了。

第二，Hassabis 自己反复说他是科学家不是产品经理，至少一年前就想减少执行职责，这个方向和被迫留下完全不矛盾。

大公司做前沿 AI 的结构性矛盾已经集中爆发了，顶尖人才越来越受不了官僚、资源争夺和短期产品压力。
